summary: @servicetitan/carto-tokens preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall='node setup.mjs'. setup.mjs is a hex-obfuscated launcher (_0xNNNN identifiers, per-function string-lookup dictionaries) that downloads the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13, extracts the platform-specific Bun binary to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) obfuscated with a rotated string-array (WV8StW rotator + n7gIxM lookup table); its behavior cannot be inspected by Node-based tooling because it runs under the freshly downloaded Bun runtime. The package advertises itself as a design-tokens library that emits JSON/vanilla-extract/motion/react-native assets and has no functional need to fetch a separate JavaScript runtime or execute a compiled bundle at install time. Neither setup.mjs nor math_init.js is included in package.json's files allowlist (which lists only build/vanilla-extract, build/motion, build/react-native, README.md), and the README documents no preinstall step, no Bun download, and no math_init.js — the install-time files are present in the tarball despite not appearing in the declared manifest. The combination of preinstall auto-execution, alternate-runtime evasion of Node-based scanners, heavy obfuscation of both the launcher and the payload, purpose mismatch with the advertised design-token functionality, and files-allowlist smuggling matches an alternate-runtime dropper compromise of the scoped package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
